thread:
sam p: heads up — prototyping a 'cadence-sculptor' sampler for synthetic traffic. goal is apples-to-apples kernel/batching experiments where QPS ramps keep client-level burst cadence and KV warmup is controllable.

nina r: sounds good. how does this differ from existing ramp/surge generators?

sam p: two main diffs — 1) per-client finite-state machine (idle/warm/active) with TTLs so prefix/KV cache state is realistic, 2) ramp shapes use lanczos smoothing + Poisson jitter to avoid aliasing and produce realistic long-tail inter-arrival times. also explicit kernel-hint tagging so we can force the runtime to take a specific kernel path for comparison.

omar_k: for KV warmup are you planning deterministic priming or probabilistic? deterministic is easier for apples-to-apples but maybe less realistic.

sam p: both. generator has a "preplay" mode that deterministically issues prefix-only requests per client to populate KV, and a "stochastic-warm" mode that follows an exponential backoff for first hits. test plan: compare identical runs with/without preplay.

lucy: dropping a config proto for the generator (WIP):

```yaml
generator:
  clients: 10000
  concurrency_per_client: 1
  seed: 42
  ramp:
    shape: lanczos_sawtooth
    period_seconds: 300
    min_qps: 0.5
    max_qps: 120
    jitter: poisson
  kv:
    preplay: true
    preplay_prefixes_per_client: 3
    ttl_seconds: 900
  batching:
    batch_hold_ms: 8
    max_batch_tokens: 2048
  kernel_hint:
    prefer_attention_kernel: "autogen_v2"
    tag_runs: true
```

jordan: ran a quick dev cluster sweep (g4 ded). baseline (batch_hold_ms=5) -> p95=42ms, p99=128ms. with batch_hold_ms=10 we saw p95=46ms (+9%), p99=148ms (+15%) but throughput increased ~6% under peak QPS. KV preplay dropped initial tail (first 60s p99) by ~30%.

perf-bot: CI: perf/regression detected on PR #5123 — p99 increased by 12% in replay harness (compare ref 1755554321 -> current 1777777777).

nina r: can we capture kernel_selection_counter and kv_miss_rate per-run? those would be critical to attribute regresses to kernel fallback vs cache misses.

sam p: yes — adding metrics plan: [kernel_selection_counter, batch_size_histogram, kv_miss_rate, kv_hit_latency, prefix_warm_fraction]. will export as tags per run + include seed in metadata for reproducibility.

omar_k: also suggest a "microburst_injector" mode — inject short 50-200ms high-QPS pulses per small subset of clients to stress kernel handoff and batching warmup.

sam p: good call. microburst params will be: pulse_qps_factor, pulse_duration_ms, target_client_ratio. will run matrix: pulse_factor {4,8,16} x client_ratio {0.1%, 1%, 5%}.

lucy: quick note on measurement: use histogram buckets for tail (1ms resolution up to 500ms, then log scale). avoid just mean/p95 — tails hide kernel adaptation problems.

jordan: next steps: 1) land generator binary in infra/bench; 2) run 3 seeds for each matrix cell; 3) upload metrics to perf dashboard with kernel+kv tags; 4) correlate with recent perf/regression (#5123).

sam p: assigning: lucy -> config + perf dashboard tags, omar_k -> KV preplay implementation, jordan -> run matrix on staging, nina r -> write experiment hypothesis and success criteria. I'll triage PR once we have initial results. :thumbsup:

sam p: attaching a short checklist for run reproducibility:
- ensure seed is logged and immutable per run
- capture runtime kernel version and selection policy
- capture batch_hold_ms and max_batch_tokens
- capture KV primary hit/miss counters
- attach raw inter-arrival histograms

nina r: if we see regressions that correlate with kernel selection flips, we should auto-run a kernel-isolate test (force-run both kernels for same trace) to measure delta.

sam p: agreed — adding kernel-isolate test to plan. target to have first report by EOD Friday.

jordan: pinging infra for a small fleet: @infra-team can we get 6x g4s for 4 hours Friday?

perf-bot: reminder: please tag runs with `repro-seed:<seed>` so CI can link failures.

sam p: thanks all — will update thread with run links and dashboard soon.
